text:
sam: Heads-up, seeing small bursts of east-west packet drops in the gpu-pool in us-west-2 starting ~02:30 UTC. Affects long seq grpc streams (trainer -> parameter-server).

jia: saw a couple retries in ingestion logs, p99 wall time for checkpoint push jumped. Can you paste the tail logs? :eyes:

sam: pastebin of tcpdump and kube events: 
```
15:30:12.345678 IP 10.10.2.45.43212 > 10.10.5.12.50051: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12389, ack 9876, win 29200, length 44
15:30:12.345690 IP 10.10.2.45 > 10.10.5.12: ICMP frag needed and DF set (mtu=8972)
15:30:12.348001 IP 10.10.5.12.50051 > 10.10.2.45.43212: Flags [R.], seq 0, ack 12389, win 0, length 0
```
Events: kubelet killed sidecar due to liveness after repeated GRPC timeouts.\n```\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n```

ow investigating offload/MTU mismatch.

owen: interesting — MTU on node overlay dev is 8972? we use 9000 on host, 8972 on vni sometimes from GENEVE header. Could be PMTU drops from underlay path.

morgan: quick checks: can you run `ss -ti` on both endpoints and `ethtool -k ens5` on host? I've seen TSO/GSO bugs cause reassembly failures when encap changes sizes.

sam: running checks now, results: `ethtool -k ens5` -> gso: on, tso: on, gro: on. `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc` = 0.

jia: do we have RDMA nodes involved? RDMA offloads behave differently with encapsulation.

sam: these pods are on GPU nodes with mlx5 (rdma enabled) but traffic is TCP grpc, not RDMA. NIC firmware is 14.32.2000.

owen: send a quick iperf3 native between two pods (hostNetwork=false) and also from host-to-host, to see if fragmentation correlates with encapsulated payload size.

sam: iperf3 results: pod->pod small payloads fine. With -M 8900 (set MSS) we drop ~0.6% packets every 10s for bursts. host->host raw path no drops.

morgan: that points to encap boundary. Are we running kernel 5.15 on nodes? older kernels had geneve reassembly issues with skb fragments and offloads.

sam: kernel 5.15.61. I also pulled dmesg: `geneve: failed to consume skb fragment, err=-12` repeated.

jia: :thinking_face: err=-12 is -ENOMEM in kernel land, could be skbuff frag allocation failing under burst. Any memory pressure on network stack? `cat /proc/slabinfo | grep skbuff`?

sam: slabinfo looks normal, but `sysctl net.core.netdev_budget` is default. bumping RX processing budget might help. Trying `sysctl -w net.core.netdev_budget=600` on a node to see triage.

owen: also try disabling GSO/TCP segmentation offload on the tunnel device to force software segmentation as a test: `ip link set genev0 type geneve ..` or `ethtool -K genev0 tso off gso off gro off` (if device shows up).

morgan: if that drops disappear it's an offload interaction. If not, maybe the underlay MTU path has an MTU hole for some ECMP path. Check `tracepath` between hosts to verify PMTU.

sam: did the tso/gso off on genev0 - burst gone in 5m of testing. Re-enabled on a control node and burst resurfaced.

jia: good repro. So likely bug in NIC offload + geneve handling. What's firmware/driver?

sam: mlx5_core 5.15.61 driver, fw 14.32.2000. I filed a bug with vendor, attached tcpdump and the `dmesg` fragments. Ticket #INFRA-1429.

owen: short-term mitigation: disable GSO/TSO on geneve across gpu-pool nodes, and ramp net.core.netdev_budget as precaution. Rollout via daemonset (ethtool -K on the tunnel iface) or host-level sysctl. We'll also add a node-label-based kube-scheduler constraint to avoid mixing with other pools.

morgan: what's perf hit? GSO off cost measured?

sam: rough numbers: p95 token latency +6-8% under normal load, cost is modest vs trainer timeouts. I'll draft an ops playbook with steps and rollback.

jia: add an automated alert for geneve dmesg pattern and p99 grpc retries so we can auto-detect early.

encap-bot: Deploy plan created: disable-gso-geneve-gpu-pool v1 -> rollout 20% -> 100% after 30m; playbook attached. :white_check_mark:

sam: plan looks good. rolling to 20% now. keeping this thread for notes and followups.
morgan: postmortem checklist: vendor buglink, kernel upgrade plan, perf regression numbers, automated alert rules, revert steps.

owen: thanks all, good catch. we'll track INFRA-1429 in the backlog and schedule firmware/driver tests in the lab. :thumbsup:
